consensus_summary: Primary meaning is advanced/mature spiritual teaching (solid food) for grown believers, contrasted with milk as elementary doctrine for spiritual infants (chiefly 1 Cor 3:1-2; Heb 5:12-14). Common alternatives include doing God’s will as nourishment (John 4), Christian liberty over food, and Christ’s flesh as true meat (John 6).
book_summary: Meat is the word obeyed to completeness (doing the will of God, equated with the word). Milk and meat are one substance in two states—the word received versus the word done—chewed/tasted as the ear tries words, given in due season, yielding senses exercised to discern.
consensus_core_identification: advanced spiritual teaching / solid food for the mature (vs milk as elementary instruction)
book_core_identification: the word obeyed/done to completeness (vs milk as the word merely received)
boundary_disagreement: Book reclassifies the milk/meat pair from a content/maturity distinction (elementary vs advanced doctrine) to a reception-versus-obedience distinction on the same word; elevates the John 4 ‘do the will’ sense from secondary alternative to definitional core and reinterprets maturity language (Heb 5:14) as fruit of practice rather than readiness for deeper teaching.
material_contradiction: Consensus treats meat as deeper teaching content suited to the mature and milk as first principles; book asserts they are identical substance in two states (received vs done) and identifies meat principally as obedience/practice. These cannot both be true of the same symbolic referent.
rationale: Minimum cores conflict: advanced doctrine versus word-done/obedience. Book’s explicit claim that milk and meat are one substance in two states replaces rather than narrows or broadens the consensus’s elementary-versus-advanced teaching referent. John 4 appears in consensus only as a common alternative, not as the redefinition of the milk/meat pair. Accepting the book therefore requires rejecting the consensus identification.
strongest_objection: Heb 5:12–14 frames ‘strong meat’ against remaining at ‘first principles of the oracles of God’ and failing to become teachers—an explicit content/maturity contrast the book re-uses without addressing, substituting a reception/obedience schema instead.
